title: Last week's promise, and an application
text: Last week I told you the real numbers would come from the model itself before the meeting. They did and they are printed on a card inside an application that now runs on a laptop with no server and no account. This is sigh. Here is what it promised and here is what it shipped. So what is it? A desktop

title: What shipped — inside the bundle
text: Application. 84 megabytes to download 176 once it is installed. Apple silicon Mac OS 1015 and up. Inside there is a rust shell, a Python service, the enh runtime and the detector itself. 36 megabytes of weights. Nothing in that list reaches for a server. And it

title: One image in, one box out
text: Behaves the way a field tool should. One image in a box drawn where the bird is. 82% on that box and a line underneath saying highlighted areas show where a loon was found. Not a score on its own a place. The history page keeps the earlier checks on your own disc. Here is

title: The card the promise was about
text: The card. The promise was about precision 93%. When it calls something a loon, it is almost always right. Recall 80. Mean average precision at 50 89. and the strict one 50 through 9561. Four numbers off the checkpoint itself, not a hand count this time. Two of those four

title: Two definitions that differ by one term
text: Are a trade and the trade has a shape. Precision divides the true finds by everything it called a loon. Recall divides the same true finds by every loon that was really there. One number balances them. The harmonic mean 86. The card does not print it. I computed it from the two it does. But 80% recall has

title: One loon in five
text: A plain meaning. One loon in five the model says nothing about. And there is a dial for it in the card. Confidence threshold 0.25. Drop it and you find more birds and more read beds. Hold it and the misses stay. That is a decision to make, not a bug to fix. So one page the promise is kept.

title: Verdict — promise kept, one number open
text: Four numbers from the checkpoint inside the app. The detector left the notebook and runs on a laptop. It calls itself a prototype on every screen. And one loon in five is still unreported. That is next week. Your turn. If you have a

title: Your turn
text: Model that only works in a notebook, try this before you demo it again. Put it in something a colleague can open with no terminal and no account.
